1.1 The Indian Trade Union Act, 1926

concepts: The Act as the foundational statute on trade unions
why a special statute was enacted for collective organisation of workmen
the Act's position alongside the other prescribed labour statutes.
provisions: The Act by name and year of enactment (1926). *The syllabus states no section numbers
any section cited in an answer must be verified against the bare Act — see Section E and Section H.*
distinctions: Trade union as a collective body versus an individual workman
registered versus unregistered trade union (developed in U1-T03 and U1-T04).
guidance.approach: Open with the Act's role in recognising collective organisation; give the year and objective; then lead into the topics that follow (history, registration, rights).

referredCases: Rangaswami and Another Vs. Registrar of Trade Unions, AIR 1962
"Rangaswami and Another Vs. Registrar of Trade Unions, AIR 1962 Mad. 231" — spelling and citation reproduced exactly.

topics.title: 1.2 History of trade union movement in India, trade unionism, need, objects, types and functions.

concepts: Growth of the trade union movement in India
the meaning and purpose of trade unionism
why trade unions are needed
their objects
types of unions
functions performed by unions.
provisions: No section number is stated. The topic is conceptual/historical and is anchored by the "objects" of a registered trade union, which the Act treats as a permitted object — verify against the bare Act before citing a provision.
distinctions: Need versus objects versus functions
types of trade unions (e.g., craft/industrial, general/occupational) — treat as classification explained in standard texts, not as a statutory classification in this syllabus.
guidance.approach: Use a chronological line for the movement, then a structured list for need/objects/types/functions; avoid presenting textbook classifications as statutorily prescribed.

referredCases: Rangaswami and Another Vs. Registrar of Trade Unions, AIR 1962
"Rangaswami and Another Vs. Registrar of Trade Unions, AIR 1962 Mad. 231" — spelling and citation reproduced exactly.

topics.title: 1.3 Registration of trade unions, rights and privileges of a registered trade union, advantages of registration.

concepts: The process of registration
the legal status conferred by registration
rights and privileges that flow from registration
the practical and legal advantages of registration.
provisions: Registration, rights and privileges of a registered trade union — named by subject matter only
no section numbers in the source. Verify before citing.
distinctions: Registered trade union versus unregistered association
"rights" versus "privileges" versus "advantages of registration"
registration as a status-conferring act rather than the creation of the union itself.
guidance.approach: Define registration, list the advantages, then connect to the *Rangaswami* case; keep rights (U1-T03) and immunities (U1-T04) clearly separated.

referredCases: Rangaswami and Another Vs. Registrar of Trade Unions, AIR 1962
"Rangaswami and Another Vs. Registrar of Trade Unions, AIR 1962 Mad. 231" — spelling and citation reproduced exactly.

topics.title: 1.4 Rights, privileges, liabilities and immunities of a registered trade union, amalgamation and dissolution of trade unions.

concepts: The full legal position of a registered trade union — rights, privileges, liabilities and immunities
the mechanisms of amalgamation and dissolution.
provisions: Rights, privileges, liabilities and immunities
amalgamation
dissolution — subject-matter only
no section numbers stated. Verify against the bare Act.
distinctions: Rights/privileges versus liabilities versus immunities
amalgamation (combination of unions) versus dissolution (ending of a union)
the trade union's corporate-style capacities versus those of its office-bearers.
guidance.approach: Use a four-part structure — rights, privileges/immunities, liabilities, then amalgamation and dissolution; give a short note on each.

referredCases: Rangaswami and Another Vs. Registrar of Trade Unions, AIR 1962
"Rangaswami and Another Vs. Registrar of Trade Unions, AIR 1962 Mad. 231" — spelling and citation reproduced exactly.

topics.title: 1.5 Penalties and procedure, collective bargaining and trade disputes

concepts: Penalties and procedural machinery under the Act
the concept and importance of collective bargaining
trade disputes as the subject matter of collective bargaining.
provisions: Penalties and procedure under the Act
collective bargaining and trade disputes — no section numbers stated. Note that the detailed law of "industrial disputes" is separately prescribed in Unit U2
do not conflate the two.
distinctions: "Trade disputes" (this topic) versus "industrial dispute" as defined under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (U2-T01)
penalties versus procedural provisions
collective bargaining versus adjudication.
guidance.approach: Define collective bargaining, contrast it with adjudication, then bridge to Unit U2; note that penalties belong to this Act, not the Industrial Disputes Act.

appropriate government (central vs. state)

"manufacturing process" as a threshold test
occupier versus manager/owner
